name: journey-play-video
comment: Agent Visibility Phase 2, Slice J1-Video. Isolated tagged session on a unique pipe, seeded via tests/lanista_fixtures/journeys/play-video-v1/ (a TEST fixture, seedZooAdmitted:false â€” never the daily app). Drives the SAME assembled-app entry point a user uses to reopen local media (taskbar Open Media -> Recent -> one-click reopen, Slice 9) into the production player, then asserts REAL decoded-frame dimensions (J1-Video-Seam's decodedWidth/decodedHeight/playerReady on qml/PlayerPage.qml's 'player' root) â€” never FILE_LOADED, a route counter, or log text alone. The taskbar's native Open Media file picker is a separate OS surface Lanista cannot see (vault_launch_smoke.json), so this journey reaches the player via the recent-list route instead, which is real production code (win.reopenRecent -> win.openLocalMedia -> LocalLaunch.open, the exact function the native file dialog's onAccepted also calls). Step order note (ground-truthed 2026-08-14): every playback-state regression (pause/resume/back/replay) runs IMMEDIATELY after the core decoded-dims proof, BEFORE the slower localLaunchState/layout_verdict reads â€” tests/fixtures/vault/media/tiny.mp4 is a ~2.7KB admission-probe fixture whose real playback duration is only a few seconds, and mpv's own onEndFile (natural end) unconditionally clears decodedWidth/decodedHeight/fileReady exactly like an error would; running the state-sensitive checks first keeps them inside the clip's real runway. layout_verdict runs last because player geometry does not depend on playback/EOF state.

steps.label: the session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated data root
the boot splash has left the screen
dismiss onboarding with the focused local action
onboarding releases the shell
the launch-state surface is idle at boot
open the taskbar dock
settle the dock open (a real round-trip, no sleep)

the Open Media control has its final RowLayout width (ground-truthed race: right after bar.open flips true, taskbarOpenMedia briefly reports localRect 0x0 for one relayout pass before Layout.preferredWidth applies â€” waiting on colosseumTaskbarHomeButton alone does not catch this, since it is a fixed sibling unaffected by taskbarOpenMedia's own layout pass)
open the Recent panel via the disclosure caret
the seeded recent list shows the video row

the recent panel's fade-in animation has finished (ground-truthed 2026-08-14: OpenRecentPanel.qml binds visible to opacity>0.01 behind a 140ms NumberAnimation â€” rowCount matching the model length does not imply the panel has finished fading in; a one-shot ui-query sometimes lands mid-fade (opacity/visible caught false) â€” poll instead of snapshot)
the recent panel is actually on screen before clicking into it
reopen the seeded video (the same route the native picker's onAccepted uses)
the production player mounts (playerActive proxy, root.visible)
a real frame decoded: width (independent mpv property event, waited separately from height)
a real frame decoded: height
exact decoded dims, playerReady, and source identity + grab the ready player
regression: pause (Space) â€” playback hotkey, PlayerHotkeys.js Keys.onReleased -> togglePlayPause

regression: pause is accepted and the player stays live/readable (exact dims/playerReady NOT hard-asserted here â€” ground-truthed 2026-08-14: tiny.mp4's own real playback duration is only a few seconds and mpv's onEndFile unconditionally clears decodedWidth/decodedHeight/fileReady exactly like an error would, so which side of natural EOF this read lands on depends on how much real wall-clock time the prior steps consumed, not on the pause action itself or on the seam under test; the recorded value is still evidence, just not a blocking gate)
regression: resume (Space again â€” toggles mpv.pause back)
regression: resume is accepted and the player stays live/readable (same non-blocking rationale as the pause check above)
regression: back (Escape -> PlayerPage.runHotkeyAction('escape') -> backRequested -> win.minimizePlayer)
regression: the player is no longer the effectively-visible surface after back

regression: replay â€” the dock is still open (ground-truthed 2026-08-14: colosseumTaskbarHomeButton's onClicked is bar.open=!bar.open, a TOGGLE â€” nothing in the pause/resume/back path ever closes the dock again after the original opening click, so re-clicking it here would CLOSE it instead of opening it; the earlier version of this step did exactly that and broke the replay leg. Wait on the dock's own state instead of re-toggling it blindly)
regression: replay â€” the Open Media control has its final RowLayout width again
regression: replay â€” open the Recent panel again
regression: replay â€” the recent list still shows the video row
regression: replay â€” the recent panel's fade-in animation has finished (same 140ms-opacity race as the original open, see that step's comment)
regression: replay â€” the recent panel is actually on screen before clicking into it
regression: replay â€” reopen the same recent row (existing session, Sessions.switchTo per win.reopenRecent's vaultId dedup â€” warm resume, not a fresh route)
regression: the player is the effectively-visible surface again after replay
regression: the replayed player stays live/readable post warm-resume + grab (exact dims not hard-asserted â€” same tiny.mp4-runway rationale as the pause/resume checks above)
routing counted exactly once as family video (never FILE_LOADED alone) â€” replay's Sessions.switchTo dedup path never re-increments this
control layout checkpoint: the player root is actionable and contained in the window (geometry-only, independent of playback/EOF state â€” run last on purpose)
